title: TwoSampleQuadraticPerceptron.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Strict binary separation in bilinear parameters: m(b;(v,a))=a⟨v,b⟩ or m(b;((a₁,a₂),v))=a₁⟨b,v⟩+a₂⟨shift(b),v⟩. The feasible parameter set need not be convex; no scalar minimization objective is specified.

oracle.label: component_gradient
oracle.details: Each oracle call returns the exact parameter gradients of both signed sample margins, ∇θm(D.positive;θ) and −∇θm(D.negative;θ), bundled in one reply. Answers are independent of history and seeds; there is no oracle error or sampling noise.

oracle.label: function_value
oracle.details: The same call also returns both exact signed margins. One budget unit counts this entire joint value-and-gradient reply, rather than each sample evaluation separately.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: Features belong to ℝᵈ with the Euclidean inner product. Parameters belong to ℝᵈ×ℝ or ℝ²×ℝᵈ. Convolution uses a cyclic coordinate shift.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Exactly two oppositely labeled samples have norms at most radius. The two-layer case requires positive sample inner product and a nonzero orthogonal component. The convolutional case requires a positive constant first sample, positive mean of the second sample, and a nonzero smooth component. Spectral coordinates satisfy first,second≥gain, couplingLower≤coupling≤couplingUpper, and, for convolution, slow≥slowLower. At initialization, with c=coordinates(start) and σ=−sign(c.z), require |c.r+c.y|≤ratio|c.r−c.y|, |c.z|≥depthLower, σ(c.p+c.q)≥wedgeLower, σ(c.p−c.q)≥0, and 2σc.p+2|c.z|≤size. All scalar bounds are positive, couplingLower≤couplingUpper, and ratio≥1. Only model, dimension, radius, and start are public; the remaining bounds are hidden. Allowed algorithms use a fixed positive step, update using the first nonpositive signed margin with priority to the positive sample, and output the current parameter.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/TwoSampleQuadraticPerceptron.lean: InClass, coordinates, eigenvalues, Params, Public, publicOf, family, spec.valid, spec.admissible; LongTails/Template.lean: Convergence.

accuracy.label: feasibility
accuracy.details: The final output θ must satisfy m(D.positive;θ)>0 and m(D.negative;θ)<0 simultaneously. No epsilon, prescribed positive margin, norm tolerance, or objective-gap criterion is present.

accuracy.label: deterministic
accuracy.details: Separation is required for every combined algorithm/oracle seed, including probability-zero seeds, after execution with the supplied fixed oracle budget.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: This is a specialized two-example bilinear separation problem with spectral and initialization restrictions, hidden quantitative bounds, a bundled exact oracle, and a prescribed update family. Repository files and local proofs were not inspected. The absence of a qualifying reference is not a novelty claim.

descriptionHtml:
Two-Sample Quadratic Perceptron

We study strict separation of two labeled vectors b+,b−∈Rd by a quadratic perceptron with score F(b;θ). The parameter θ belongs to Rd×R for the two-layer model or R2×Rd for the convolutional model. The data have norms at most R>0 and satisfy model-specific geometric and spectral bounds; a given initialization θ0 satisfies signed wedge, depth, and size conditions. The oracle returns both signed scores and their parameter-gradient directions exactly. A fixed positive-step perceptron updates the first misclassified sample, prioritizing b+. The goal is an output θ¯ with F(b+;θ¯)>0 and F(b−;θ¯)<0 for every realization.

Let d∈N0, with Euclidean inner product and norm on the feature space Rd. Write 1∈Rd for the all-ones vector and S for the cyclic shift, so that (Sb)i=bi−1modd when d>0; in dimension zero, S is the unique map. The two scores are F(b;(w,a))=a⟨w,b⟩(two-layer),F(b;((u,v),w))=u⟨b,w⟩+v⟨Sb,w⟩(convolutional). Their parameter-gradient directions, in the same coordinate order, are G(b;(w,a))=(ab,⟨w,b⟩),G(b;((u,v),w))=((⟨b,w⟩,⟨Sb,w⟩),ub+vSb). The algorithm receives only the model, d, R, and θ0. The remaining parameters introduced below may enter the oracle-call budget but are not algorithm inputs.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Data geometry). Both samples satisfy ∥b+∥≤R and ∥b−∥≤R. For the two-layer model, define eA=b+∥b+∥,n=b−−⟨b−,eA⟩eA,eB=n∥n∥. We require ⟨b+,b−⟩>0 and n≠0. For the convolutional model, define the mean level and the centered directions by ℓ(b)=⟨b,1⟩d,b~−=b−−ℓ(b−)1,h+=b~−+Sb~−,h−=b~−−Sb~−. We require b+=ℓ(b+)1,ℓ(b+)>0,ℓ(b−)>0,h+≠0. The admissible data necessarily have d>0; all mean levels above are taken in this case.

Assumption 2 (Spectral bounds). Let g>0, 0<c−≤c+, and s−>0. Define the model-dependent quantities (λ1,λ2,c,s)={(∥b+∥,⟨b−,eA⟩,∥n∥,0),two-layer,(ℓ(b+)2d,ℓ(b−)2d,∥h+∥/2,∥h−∥/2),convolutional. They satisfy λ1≥g,λ2≥g,c−≤c≤c+. For the convolutional model, additionally s≥s−.

Assumption 3 (Initialization geometry). Let ρ≥1 and ω,δ,M>0. For the given starting point, define coordinates (p,q,z,r,y) as follows. In the two-layer model, with θ0=(w0,a0), set p=a0,q=⟨w0,eA⟩,z=⟨w0,eB⟩,r=y=0. In the convolutional model, with θ0=((u0,v0),w0), set p=u0+v02,q=⟨w0,1⟩d,z=⟨w0,h+⟩∥h+∥,r=u0−v02,y=⟨w0,h−⟩∥h−∥. Writing σ=−sgn(z), we require |r+y|≤ρ|r−y|,|z|≥δ,σ(p+q)≥ω,σ(p−q)≥0,2σp+2|z|≤M.

Our result is algorithm-specific: we analyze the two-sample quadratic perceptron with a constant step size γ>0. At any query point θ, one oracle call returns the tuple (F(b+;θ), G(b+;θ), −F(b−;θ), −G(b−;θ)). Starting at the supplied θ0, the method follows θk+1={θk+γG(b+;θk),F(b+;θk)≤0,θk−γG(b−;θk),F(b+;θk)>0, F(b−;θk)≥0,θk,F(b+;θk)>0, F(b−;θk)<0. The step size is fixed throughout the run and may depend only on the available inputs. After K∈N0 oracle calls, the output is the current iterate θ¯=θK. The required accuracy is strict separation, F(b+;θ¯)>0,F(b−;θ¯)<0, for every realization of any algorithm or oracle randomness.

comparisonHtml:
Two labeled samples b1,b2∈Rd, ∥bi∥≤R. The width-one model is m(b;(v,c))=c⟨v,b⟩, with ⟨b1,b2⟩>0 and b2∦b1; the kernel-two model is m(b;((c1,c2),v))=c1⟨b,v⟩+c2⟨Pb,v⟩, with b1=b¯11, b¯1,b¯2>0, and (I+P)(b2−b¯21)≠0. In the setup’s coordinates and spectrum, g≤λ1,λ2, β−≤β≤β+, and the kernel-two slow eigenvalue is at least μ. All bounds R,g,β−,β+,μ,a,z,S are positive and ρ≥1. The start satisfies |r0+y0|≤ρ|r0−y0|, |z0|≥z, σ(p0+q0)≥a, σ(p0−q0)≥0, and 2σp0+2|z0|≤S. One oracle call returns exact signed margins and gradients for the two samples. The setup requires constant-step, first-violated-sample updates and the current iterate as output; (1) uses γ=1/(2R). Target: deterministically m(b1;θT)>0>m(b2;θT), also at every later step.

(2) Noisy quadratic perceptron (Tyurin 2026, Thm. 5.1, v2). Special case: kernel two, b1=1, b2=1+μe1, 0<μ≤1/10. O(dμL1L2[1+log(dL1L2μ)]) calls; success probability 1−δ. Requires h>0, γ=1/(4d), and the theorem’s tuned Gaussian perturbations. (1): Deterministic, noise-free analysis; extends to general admissible convolutional data and width one. On this dataset, matches d/μ up to unordered initialization logarithms; if r0y0≤0, gives O(1+log⁡(S/a+Sd3/2/(μ3z))) instead. (1) needs a data-dependent cone of starts; (2) covers every start with h>0.
(3) Derived bound: direct reconstruction; linear representation (Tyurin 2026, sec. 1.1). Same data and oracle, unrestricted updates. O(1): one call recovers b1,b2; construct a linear separator and represent it in either model. (1): No established improvement in problem-class complexity. Its contribution concerns the prescribed perceptron dynamics. (1) has a larger bound and restricts starts. (3) lies outside the required update family.
(4) Batch linear perceptron (Tyurin 2026, Thm. 5.2, v2). Special case: b1=1, b2=1+μe1, 0<μ≤1/2. Lower bound Ω(d/μ) paired-sample calls; step ϕ>0, initial linear weight u0∈B(0,ϕμ/(8maxi∥bi∥)). (1) retains the inherited quadratic-versus-linear method contrast; (4) is a lower bound, not a competing upper bound. Different initializations preclude an identical-start comparison.

Abbr: P: cyclic coordinate shift; b¯=d−1⟨b,1⟩; (p0,q0,z0,r0,y0): the linked setup’s coordinates of θ0; σ=−sign(z0). g: lower bound on fast coefficients λ1,λ2; β−,β+: coupling bounds; μ: slow-eigenvalue lower bound (also the sample perturbation in (2), (4)); a,z,S: cone-margin, depth and size bounds; ρ: slow-coordinate ratio bound. Width one has r0=y0=0 and permits ρ=1. h=|⟨θ0,vμ,+⟩|, with vμ,+ the unit positive slow eigenvector of the signed second-sample quadratic form; δ∈(0,1): failure probability; L1=1+log⁡(∥θ0∥2/(δ3h2)), L2=1+log⁡(d∥θ0∥2/(μh2)). Costs count exact margin-and-gradient queries for the two samples; counting individual sample queries changes only a universal factor.

source:
import LongTails.Template
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.PiL2

open OracleTemplate
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.TwoSampleQuadraticPerceptron

inductive Model where
  | twoLayer
  | conv

abbrev Features (d : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)

abbrev Space : Model → ℕ → Type
  | .twoLayer, d => Features d × ℝ
  | .conv, d => (ℝ × ℝ) × Features d

noncomputable def shift {d : ℕ} (x : Features d) : Features d :=
  WithLp.toLp 2 fun i => x ((finRotate d).symm i)

noncomputable def ones (d : ℕ) : Features d := WithLp.toLp 2 fun _ => 1

noncomputable def margin : (m : Model) → (d : ℕ) → Features d → Space m d → ℝ
  | .twoLayer, _, b, θ => ⟪θ.1, b⟫ * θ.2
  | .conv, _, b, θ => θ.1.1 * ⟪b, θ.2⟫ + θ.1.2 * ⟪shift b, θ.2⟫

noncomputable def direction : (m : Model) → (d : ℕ) → Features d → Space m d → Space m d
  | .twoLayer, _, b, θ => (θ.2 • b, ⟪θ.1, b⟫)
  | .conv, _, b, θ => ((⟪b, θ.2⟫, ⟪shift b, θ.2⟫), θ.1.1 • b + θ.1.2 • shift b)

noncomputable def move : (m : Model) → (d : ℕ) → Space m d → ℝ → Space m d → Space m d
  | .twoLayer, _, θ, γ, g => θ + γ • g
  | .conv, _, θ, γ, g => θ + γ • g

noncomputable def negate : (m : Model) → (d : ℕ) → Space m d → Space m d
  | .twoLayer, _, g => -g
  | .conv, _, g => -g

structure Data (d : ℕ) where
  positive : Features d
  negative : Features d

structure Reply (m : Model) (d : ℕ) where
  first : ℝ
  firstDirection : Space m d
  second : ℝ
  secondDirection : Space m d

noncomputable def answer (m : Model) (d : ℕ) (D : Data d) (θ : Space m d) : Reply m d where
  first := margin m d D.positive θ
  firstDirection := direction m d D.positive θ
  second := -margin m d D.negative θ
  secondDirection := negate m d (direction m d D.negative θ)

def Separates (m : Model) (d : ℕ) (D : Data d) (θ : Space m d) : Prop :=
  0 < margin m d D.positive θ ∧ 0 < -margin m d D.negative θ

noncomputable def axisA (d : ℕ) (D : Data d) : Features d := ‖D.positive‖⁻¹ • D.positive

noncomputable def normalPart (d : ℕ) (D : Data d) : Features d :=
  D.negative - ⟪D.negative, axisA d D⟫ • axisA d D

noncomputable def axisB (d : ℕ) (D : Data d) : Features d := ‖normalPart d D‖⁻¹ • normalPart d D

noncomputable def level (d : ℕ) (x : Features d) : ℝ := ⟪x, ones d⟫ / d

noncomputable def detrended (d : ℕ) (D : Data d) : Features d :=
  D.negative - level d D.negative • ones d

noncomputable def smooth (d : ℕ) (D : Data d) : Features d := detrended d D + shift (detrended d D)

noncomputable def rough (d : ℕ) (D : Data d) : Features d := detrended d D - shift (detrended d D)

structure Coordinates where
  p : ℝ
  q : ℝ
  z : ℝ
  r : ℝ
  y : ℝ

noncomputable def coordinates : (m : Model) → (d : ℕ) → Data d → Space m d → Coordinates
  | .twoLayer, d, D, θ =>
      ⟨θ.2, ⟪θ.1, axisA d D⟫, ⟪θ.1, axisB d D⟫, 0, 0⟩
  | .conv, d, D, θ =>
      ⟨(θ.1.1 + θ.1.2) / Real.sqrt 2, ⟪θ.2, ones d⟫ / Real.sqrt d,
        ⟪θ.2, smooth d D⟫ / ‖smooth d D‖, (θ.1.1 - θ.1.2) / Real.sqrt 2,
        ⟪θ.2, rough d D⟫ / ‖rough d D‖⟩

structure Spectrum where
  first : ℝ
  second : ℝ
  coupling : ℝ
  slow : ℝ

noncomputable def eigenvalues : (m : Model) → (d : ℕ) → Data d → Spectrum
  | .twoLayer, d, D => ⟨‖D.positive‖, ⟪D.negative, axisA d D⟫, ‖normalPart d D‖, 0⟩
  | .conv, d, D => ⟨level d D.positive * Real.sqrt (2 * d), level d D.negative * Real.sqrt (2 * d),
      ‖smooth d D‖ / Real.sqrt 2, ‖rough d D‖ / Real.sqrt 2⟩

def InClass : (m : Model) → (d : ℕ) → Data d → Prop
  | .twoLayer, d, D => 0 < ⟪D.positive, D.negative⟫ ∧ normalPart d D ≠ 0
  | .conv, d, D => D.positive = level d D.positive • ones d ∧ 0 < level d D.positive ∧
      0 < level d D.negative ∧ smooth d D ≠ 0

structure Params where
  model : Model
  dimension : ℕ
  radius : ℝ
  start : Space model dimension
  gain : ℝ
  couplingLower : ℝ
  couplingUpper : ℝ
  slowLower : ℝ
  ratio : ℝ
  wedgeLower : ℝ
  depthLower : ℝ
  size : ℝ

structure Public where
  model : Model
  dimension : ℕ
  radius : ℝ
  start : Space model dimension

def publicOf (p : Params) : Public := ⟨p.model, p.dimension, p.radius, p.start⟩

def family (P : Public) (A : Algorithm (Space P.model P.dimension) (Reply P.model P.dimension)
    (Space P.model P.dimension)) : Prop :=
  ∃ (point : A.State → Space P.model P.dimension) (γ : ℝ), 0 < γ ∧
    (∀ seed, point (A.initial seed) = P.start) ∧
    (∀ state, A.query state = (0, point state)) ∧
    (∀ state reply, point (A.update state reply) =
      if reply.first ≤ 0 then move P.model P.dimension (point state) γ reply.firstDirection
      else if reply.second ≤ 0 then move P.model P.dimension (point state) γ reply.secondDirection
      else point state) ∧
    (∀ state, A.output state = point state)

noncomputable def spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Public
  Instance P := Data P.dimension
  Query P := Space P.model P.dimension
  Reply P := Reply P.model P.dimension
  Output P := Space P.model P.dimension
  publicInput := publicOf
  valid p := 0 < p.radius ∧ 0 < p.gain ∧ 0 < p.couplingLower ∧ p.couplingLower ≤ p.couplingUpper ∧
    0 < p.slowLower ∧ 1 ≤ p.ratio ∧ 0 < p.wedgeLower ∧ 0 < p.depthLower ∧ 0 < p.size
  admissible p D oracle :=
    let c := coordinates p.model p.dimension D p.start
    let s := eigenvalues p.model p.dimension D
    let σ := -(SignType.sign c.z : ℝ)
    InClass p.model p.dimension D ∧ ‖D.positive‖ ≤ p.radius ∧ ‖D.negative‖ ≤ p.radius ∧
    p.gain ≤ s.first ∧ p.gain ≤ s.second ∧
    p.couplingLower ≤ s.coupling ∧ s.coupling ≤ p.couplingUpper ∧
    (p.model = .conv → p.slowLower ≤ s.slow) ∧
    |c.r + c.y| ≤ p.ratio * |c.r - c.y| ∧
    p.depthLower ≤ |c.z| ∧ p.wedgeLower ≤ σ * (c.p + c.q) ∧ 0 ≤ σ * (c.p - c.q) ∧
    2 * σ * c.p + 2 * |c.z| ≤ p.size ∧
    ∀ k query seed, oracle.answer k query seed = answer p.model p.dimension D query.2
  successful p D output _ := ∀ ω, Separates p.model p.dimension D (output ω)
  allowedAlgorithm := family

end LongTails.Setups.TwoSampleQuadraticPerceptron
